speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where your neck and arm pain is located, when it started, and list all symptoms like paresthesias or weakness. Please also note if any specific movements make the pain worse.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the chronic burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive hand weakness are concerning. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, could you specify if the weakness is more pronounced in the hands or arms, and whether you have noticed any changes in bowel or bladder function? Additionally, have you experienced any numbness in the groin area or difficulty walking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The combination of progressive weakness, paresthesias, absent reflexes, and fasciculations in the context of chronic burning pain is highly suggestive of motor neuron disease. I am requesting immediate neuroimaging of the cervical spine and an MRI of the brain to rule out compressive myelopathy or other structural causes. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI, Brain_MRI.
